newsitem.title: UK: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SETS THE PACE IN QUALIFYING.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SETS THE PACE IN QUALIFYING.

text.p: Michael Doohan, who should clinch his fourth 500cc motorcycling world title in a row at the British Grand Prix on Sunday, dominated the opening qualifying session on Friday.

The Australian took his Honda round the circuit in a fastest time of one minute 33.579 seconds, well ahead of Italian Doriano Romboni's Aprilia in 1:33.807, and with his sights firmly on an eighth consecutive pole
Spaniard Carlos Checa was third fastest in 1:33.873 on his reserve bike after crashing earlier in the day.
Japanese Honda rider Tadayuki Okada completed the provisional front row of the grid with a time of 1:33.907.
Doohan said the lack of grip on the circuit had slowed everyone and he predicted a slow race on Sunday.
"Things are just not all that good out there although I must say that it seems to be better for me than some of the other guys. We go slower here each year and that is simply due to the lack of grip.
"The situation seemed to deteriorate from this morning to this afternoon and if we do go quicker tomorrow it will be because we are understanding the surface conditions better."
The 500cc lap record at Donington was last broken by now-retired American Kevin Schwantz in 1991.
Doohan merely needs to finish in the top six to win the title and so should not be too bothered.
Romboni also complained of a lack of grip and pointed his finger at the nearby East Midlands airport as a possible explanation for the problem.

"The only problem is on the fastest part where the bike slides a lot because the surface seems to be dirty. I often wonder whether this is caused by the fuel that is coming from aircraft landing at the airport," he said.
France's Jean-Michel Bayle, riding the British-built Modenas, was fifth fastest after crashing in the morning's open practice session when he was third fastest.
Suzuki's Australian rider Anthony Gobert was 18th fastest after falling, a dismal showing for his suffering team but he at least had one of the more original excuses.
"My main problem is that I need a good night's sleep," he said. "I missed my plane from Australia so I only arrived yesterday, 24 hours late and I'm a bit tired today."
The final qualifying session is on Saturday.
